title: 2026 Georgia gubernatorial election
description: Georgia voters will elect a governor in 2026 in an open-seat race because Republican Gov. Brian Kemp is term-limited and cannot run again. The contest is expected to be a major test of partisan control in a closely divided state that has been competitive in recent statewide elections. Major issues in the race include taxes, health care, education, and the state's broader political direction, based on candidates' campaign messaging. The eventual nominees will also be shaped by the state's recent history of narrow statewide margins and intense turnout battles.

Healthcare.stance: Keisha Lance Bottoms says she would lower health care costs by expanding Medicaid, ending Georgia Pathways, and replacing it with broader coverage. Her plan also includes stabilizing rural hospitals, expanding telehealth and EMS access, reducing prescription drug costs, and strengthening mental health and maternal health services.

Economy.stance: Her economic agenda emphasizes small business support, workforce development, and housing affordability. She has proposed restructuring the Department of Economic Development, creating an Office of Small Business, expanding loan and grant programs, and establishing an affordable housing trust fund.

Climate/Energy.stance: Keisha Lance Bottoms says she would treat climate and environmental policy as a governing priority by investing in flood mitigation, brownfield redevelopment, and water infrastructure. She also says Georgia should slow the rapid expansion of data centers to limit pressure on utility bills, water resources, and surrounding communities.

Immigration.stance: No public position found on a Georgia governor immigration platform beyond her past actions as Atlanta mayor limiting the city’s cooperation with ICE detainee housing. Her campaign issues page does not appear to include a dedicated immigration plank.

sources.title: Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms Issues Executive Order to Stop ICE Detainees

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Keisha Lance Bottoms supports universal background checks and a red flag law, and her campaign says she supports the Second Amendment. She frames gun policy as part of a broader public safety agenda that also includes prevention and reentry programs.

Foreign Policy.stance: No public position found on a dedicated foreign policy platform for the Georgia governor race. Her campaign materials focus on state issues rather than foreign policy.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Bottoms says she would oppose Georgia’s six-week abortion ban and expand abortion access. Her campaign says she would fight to restore a woman’s right to choose and protect reproductive freedom.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Bottoms says she would protect civil rights by defending reproductive freedom, pushing back on voting restrictions, protecting local election officials from political interference, and supporting broader democracy protections. Her campaign also highlights civil rights reforms and equity-focused leadership from her time as Atlanta mayor.

Tech & AI.stance: Bottoms has tied technology policy to data-center oversight, saying Georgia should slow rapid data-center expansion until impacts on water use, utility bills, and communities are better addressed. Public campaign materials do not show a detailed standalone AI platform.

Election Policy.stance: She supports expanding early voting and absentee voting, making Election Day a state holiday, and protecting local election officials from political interference. Her campaign also says she would rein in the State Election Board and push back on efforts that make voting harder.

Local Issues.stance: Her local-government agenda focuses on affordable housing, public safety, and democracy protections. She backs a Georgia Housing Fast Track, expanded renter and down payment assistance, more support for local law enforcement, and stronger flood mitigation and water infrastructure.

Education.stance: She says she would fully fund Georgia schools, modernize the state’s education funding formula, expand literacy and financial literacy, support universal childcare, eliminate the state income tax for teachers, and create a path to free technical and community college.

candidates.donor_summary: OpenSecrets shows Chris Carr raised about $3,416,399 in the 2022 cycle, with 2,778 donors, and his 2024 top industries were lawyers/law firms, commercial banks, beer/wine/liquor, and real estate. The 2024 contributor page also shows he had raised about $651,437 in that cycle at the time of the listing, making his donor base clearly concentrated in legal, financial, and business sectors. Sources: https://www.opensecrets.org/officeholders/chris-carr/summary?cycle=2022&id=43587403, https://www.opensecrets.org/officeholders/chris-carr/industries?cycle=2024&id=43587403, https://www.opensecrets.org/officeholders/chris-carr/contributors?cycle=2024&id=43587403
candidates.voting_summary: Chris Carr is Georgia's attorney general, not a legislator, so there is no legislative voting record. His public governing record is instead his executive office record, and the Georgia Attorney General's biography says he has focused on prosecuting violent crime, defending the state's election law, supporting law enforcement, and pursuing fraud cases. Sources: https://law.georgia.gov/biography-attorney-general, https://www.ballotpedia.org/Chris_Carr_(Georgia), https://justfacts.votesmart.org/candidate/175938/chris-carr

Healthcare.stance: Carr favors state-led, market-oriented health policy, including lower costs, more transparency, and improved access in rural areas. He has also opposed broad federal health-care expansions and has backed efforts to increase prescription drug pricing transparency.

Economy.stance: Carr says he wants to grow jobs, support workforce development, and keep Georgia competitive for business investment. He has also backed property-tax relief and other pro-growth policies aimed at lowering costs for residents and employers.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Carr says he supports Second Amendment rights and has defended Georgia gun laws in court. He has also indicated he is open to changes in Georgia’s gun framework and has challenged some local gun restrictions.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Carr supports Georgia’s six-week abortion ban and the state’s Heartbeat Law. He has not called for changes to those restrictions in his campaign materials reviewed.

Climate/Energy.stance: Carr opposes federal climate mandates and says Georgia should prioritize affordable, reliable energy and economic growth. His public statements emphasize a Georgia-centered approach rather than federal climate regulation.

Tech & AI.stance: Carr says Georgia should lead in AI and data-center development, pairing growth with workforce training, technical colleges, and attention to energy and water use. He supports a pro-growth approach that allows local communities to opt in to projects.

Election Policy.stance: Carr has emphasized election integrity and supported efforts to defend Georgia election laws. Public materials also show him joining litigation against noncitizen voting, but no detailed standalone election-policy platform was found.

Education.stance: Carr says Georgia should have a top-tier public education system and supports parental choice across public, private, home, and charter options. He also emphasizes early literacy, technical colleges, and preparing students for the workforce and AI-related jobs.

flags.concern: Amanda Duffy's profile reports 'no public position found' on abortion/reproductive health with high confidence (citing her official issues and platform pages). However, this is framed as a factual observation that these pages lack dedicated sections, which is accurate. The high-confidence rating here is appropriate because the absence was verified through direct inspection of campaign materials. No concern.

Jason Esteves' education section lists 'Bachelor's degree' in 'Law' and 'Juris Doctor' in 'Law', both from University of Georgia, with the B.A./B.S. appearing twice. Law is typically a graduate field (J.D.), not an undergraduate major. The cited source (Georgia legislative bio PDF) should clarify whether Esteves holds both a B.A. and a J.D., or if this is a data duplication error.
flags.suggestion: Verify against the official Georgia legislature biography PDF (https://www.legis.ga.gov/api/document/docs/default-source/bios/esteves-jason-5014.pdf) and correct any duplication or field misalignment.

flags.concern: Geoff Duncan's donor summary cites OpenSecrets data from 'the referenced cycle' (2021 and 2019) but does not clearly specify a total for his 2026 gubernatorial campaign. The summary notes his historical fundraising (~$280,752) but provides no current 2026 cycle total, unlike other candidates with more recent figures. This reflects genuine limitations in currently available data given the timing of the profile (May 2026), not a research failure.
flags.suggestion: No action needed; the gap is transparent and reflective of data availability. If 2026 FEC or state disclosure data becomes available post-primary, update with current totals.

flags.concern: Derrick Jackson's career_history array is empty (no entries), yet the summary and sources confirm he is a sitting Georgia House member (District 68) since 2023. The profile voting_source_url and summary text correctly identify him as a current legislator, but the structured career_history field should include this role.
flags.suggestion: Add a career_history entry: {"title": "Member", "organization": "Georgia House of Representatives District 68", "start_year": 2023, "end_year": null, "description": "..."}.

flags.concern: Olu Brown's Foreign Policy stance is listed with no sources and the 'sources' array is absent (not an empty array). This is a minor formatting inconsistency; the stance correctly reads 'No public position found' but lacks even a low-confidence source citation as shown in other candidates' low-confidence issues.

reviews.summary: This is a well-researched and comprehensively sourced profile of the 2026 Georgia gubernatorial race. Strengths include: (1) Consistent, neutral framing across all nine Democratic candidates and one Republican candidate; (2) Robust sourcing from official campaign websites, news outlets, and public records for policy stances; (3) Transparent documentation of gaps—where candidates have not published positions, the profile correctly flags 'no public position found' with low confidence ratings rather than speculating; (4) Accurate candidate backgrounds verified against cited sources (e.g., Keisha Lance Bottoms' mayoral tenure, Jason Esteves' state senate service, Chris Carr's attorney general role); (5) Appropriate use of high-, medium-, and low-confidence tags that reflect the depth of public information available. Minor weaknesses: some candidates (e.g., Derrick Jackson, Amanda Duffy) have sparse fundraising data or limited policy detail, but these gaps are transparently marked and reflect real campaign communication patterns rather than research failures. The generator metadata (five model IDs) is correct pipeline metadata and should not be flagged. Overall, this profile demonstrates careful adherence to epistemological standards: sources beat training data, no value-laden language is applied asymmetrically, and absences of public information are documented rather than fabricated.

reviews.summary: This is an exceptionally thorough and well-documented candidate profile. The research agent successfully navigated a complex field of candidates, maintaining high sourcing standards across official campaign sites and reputable media outlets. Each candidate’s background, including education and career history, is clearly linked to verifiable sources. The profile handles the difficulty of identifying policy stances for specific issues (like 'Foreign Policy') with transparency by explicitly stating when no public position was found, which is a hallmark of high-quality research.
